items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And then I heard Robert E. Lee wrote it on "Indian Love Call" for the band one time, Don Dunbar's band

ctx.x: with the flat five. And then I heard Robert E. Lee wrote it on "Indian Love Call" for the band one time, Don Dunbar's band, and they called it C-minor sixth with A in the bass -- which is the same thing. You see? So I was familiar with that sound way back in Mississippi.

I was aware of that sound, you know, because I had studied the chords, and I knew my chords very well. By the time I got to fourteen years old, I could play chords upside-down, back and around again, because that's the way I learned to play -- ad-lib. I didn't learn like most kids learned, by listening to the records or copping the solos off there, even though I liked things and I listened to the records. But I never copied anything off the record until this day. Not that that's really good, because you're…
